entities.name: Caradog ap Meirion
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Caradog ap Meirion reigned as the king of Gwynedd in North West Wales from approximately 754 to 798 CE. This Welsh name means Caradog son of Meirion.

He played a crucial role in the early medieval period, navigating the complex web of alliances and rivalries between various Welsh kingdoms. His reign was marked by struggles against the Viking invasions and the Saxon kingdoms to the south.

The legacy of Caradog ap Meirion can be seen in the continued influence of Gwynedd's culture and traditions in modern-day Wales. His reign also laid the groundwork for the eventual unification of Wales under a single ruler in the 13th century.

A striking statistic that highlights the impact of Caradog ap Meirion's reign is the number of Welsh speakers who still proudly speak the ancient language today. With over 700,000 people speaking Welsh, it is a testament to the enduring power of the Welsh culture that Caradog ap Meirion helped shape.

One of the most enduring cultural footprints of Caradog ap Meirion is the numerous place names that bear his name, scattered throughout Wales and beyond. From the town of Caradog in Ceredigion to the Caradog River in Pembrokeshire, his legacy lives on in the very landscape he once ruled.

In a poignant irony, Caradog ap Meirion's own death in 798 CE marked the beginning of a new era in Welsh history. His passing paved the way for the rise of the Kingdom of Seisyll, which would eventually become a major force in Welsh politics.
